questions.q: How does Grant distinguish character from personality?
a: Character is choosing values over instinct; personality is instinct
Character is fixed at birth; personality develops through practice
Character is how others see you; personality is how you see yourself
Character is learned in childhood; personality changes with age
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines personality as our basic instincts and character as our capacity to put values ahead of them.

questions.q: What does Grant mean by starting before you feel ready?
a: Comfort grows through practice rather than before it
You should wait until your skills are fully developed
You should begin with the easiest part of a project
Confidence must be built before any public attempt
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you do not need to feel comfortable first, because comfort grows as you practice your skills.

questions.q: Why does Grant recommend setting a minimum mistake target?
a: Making failure part of the plan makes it hurt less
It guarantees that you will avoid serious errors
It shows others that you are working hard
It helps you finish tasks more quickly
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests a weekly or daily mistake target so that failing feels planned and less painful.

Writing ideas on a board while others talk aloud

Holding a long meeting until everyone agrees
questions.why: Lesson 3 says people should gather ideas separately first, then use meeting time to select and refine them.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the roundabout path to progress?
a: It can feel circular but is really a slow upward spiral
It avoids setbacks by following a strict straight line
It requires abandoning your main goal for a side project
It works best only for people in the second half of life
questions.why: Lesson 2 says progress may look like wandering in circles, yet it is often a gradual climb upward.
